text:
Mark Scheifele is 33, has spent his whole career with the Jets, and is nearing 1,000 NHL games. This season has started slowly by his standards: three goals on 6.74 expected, shooting 7.7 percent, 16 points in 17 games. The looks are there, and goals usually follow chances.

He is still the setup man in Winnipeg. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 11.8 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards, and the Jets carry 52.4 percent of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice this year. The trade-off Evolving-Hockey flagged last season still deserves attention: opponents generated more with him out there than with almost any forward in the league (bottom 3 percent).

The Jets have had a rough few weeks, but Scheifele has eight points in his last five games. Our range puts his true scoring rate above what he has shown so far, and the projection lands around 93 points. Watch the goal count; it should climb.
headline: Scheifele is getting the chances, not the goals
